root_cause.text: The interrupt shadow state (int_state) written by the CPU to vmcb02 after VMRUN of L2 was not being synchronized to the cached vmcb12, causing the authoritative copy of nested VM controls to become stale and leading to incorrect interrupt shadow restoration when KVM_SET_VCPU_EVENTS precedes KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `svm->nested.ctl.int_state = svm->vmcb->control.int_state;` to `nested_sync_control_from_vmcb02()`, which is the function responsible for syncing CPU-written fields from vmcb02 to the cached vmcb12. The CVE description explicitly states that "int_state is also written by the CPU, specifically bit 0 (i.e. SVM_INTERRUPT_SHADOW_MASK) for nested VMs, but it is not sync'd to cached vmcb12," and that this omission causes the interrupt shadow to be restored to vmcb01 instead of vmcb02 when the ioctl order is reversed, potentially causing L2 to hang.

intent_record.intent_summary: Synchronize the int_state field from VMCB control block to nested control structure to prevent interrupt state desynchronization.
intent_record.what: Added a single line that copies the int_state field from svm->vmcb->control to svm->nested.ctl, positioned after similar event_inj field copies.
intent_record.how: This change ensures that the interrupt state is synchronized from the VMCB (Virtual Machine Control Block) into the nested control structure during nested VM synchronization. Previously, int_state was not being copied, which could cause the nested VM's interrupt state to become out of sync with the actual VMCB state.

bic_trace_step.commit_msg:
KVM: nSVM: synchronize VMCB controls updated by the processor on every vmexit

The control state changes on every L2->L0
bic_trace_step.code_snippet:
commit 2d8a42be0e2b15a4e0b20349f27bb8288db5ebe6
Author: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com>
Date:   Fri May 22 03:50:14 2020 -0400

    KVM: nSVM: synchronize VMCB controls updated by the processor on every vmexit
    
    The control state changes on every L2->L0 vmexit, and we will have to
    serialize it in the nested state.  So keep it up to date in svm->nested.ctl
    and just copy them back to the nested VMCB in nested_svm_vmexit.
    
    Signed-off-by: Paolo Bonzini <pbonzini@redhat.com
bic_trace_step.reason: This commit introduces the fix for the vulnerability. The new `sync_nested_vmcb_control()` function (lines 240-262) explicitly synchronizes the interrupt shadow state and other control fields from vmcb02 (svm->vmcb) back to the cached vmcb12 (svm->nested.ctl). Specifically, it copies `event_inj`, `event_inj_err`, and `int_ctl` fields with proper masking logic. The commit also modifies `nested_svm_vmexit()` to use the synchronized cached values (`svm->nested.ctl.int_ctl`, `svm->nested.ctl.event_inj`, etc.) instead of directly reading from vmcb, ensuring the authoritative copy is kept up-to-date. The vulnerable construct (stale int_state in vmcb12) is being fixed by this synchronization mechanism, not introduced.

bic_trace_step.reason: This commit INTRODUCES the fix for the vulnerability. The root cause was that interrupt shadow state (int_state) and other control fields written by the CPU to vmcb02 were not being synchronized to the cached vmcb12. The commit adds a new function `sync_nested_vmcb_control()` (lines 240-262) that explicitly synchronizes processor-written fields including event_inj, event_inj_err, and int_ctl from svm->vmcb->control to svm->nested.ctl. The function is designed to be called on every vmexit to keep the cached control state up to date. Additionally, the nested_svm_vmexit function is modified to use the synchronized cached values (svm->nested.ctl) when copying back to nested_vmcb (lines 540-543: 'nested_vmcb->control.int_ctl = svm->nested.ctl.int_ctl', etc.) instead of directly from vmcb->control. This ensures the authoritative copy of nested VM controls remains synchronized and prevents stale state issues when KVM_SET_VCPU_EVENTS precedes KVM_SET_NESTED_STATE. The vulnerable construct (unsynchronized int_state and control fields) is being FIXED by this commit, not introduced.
